text:
zara: Running into a weird intermittent hang in our sample FastAPI app after switching to httpx 0.x. Endpoint just never returns after code edit with --reload.

mike: suspect module-level AsyncClient or something creating background tasks at import. those survive parent process and confuse the child loop.

zara: we only create a client in a helper module so it's technically not top-level code, but it's executed during import by our pkg init. snippet:
```python
# sdk_boot.py
client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10)
async def ensure_ready():
    await client.get("https://example.com/health")
```

ryan: yeah that will create tasks as soon as module imported. With uvicorn --reload parent/child process semantics, the AsyncClient's background tasks end up tied to the wrong loop -> hangs or "Task was destroyed but it is pending!" at shutdown.

mike: quick repro I ran: fork the process after import, child loop fails closing client. you also see "RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop" if code calls asyncio.run in startup.

zara: our SDK currently exposes `bootstrap()` that calls `asyncio.run(_bootstrap_async())` for convenience. maybe that's part of it.

ryan: two separate UX bugs: 1) sync bootstrap that calls asyncio.run can break inside frameworks, 2) module-scope AsyncClient leaks tasks. For the SDK we should: expose an `async def bootstrap_async()` and make the sync shim run safely in a background thread instead of calling asyncio.run unconditionally.

mike: also propose shipping a small `lifespan_client` helper that returns an async contextmanager and an `install_lifespan(app, name=...)` convenience for FastAPI/Starlette so users wire it up correctly. Example:
```python
from redwood_sdk.async_utils import install_lifespan
app = FastAPI()
install_lifespan(app, client_factory=lambda: httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10))
# app.state.redwood_client available in handlers
```

zara: one more: when folks try to auto-cleanup with atexit we see "Event loop is closed" errors. We used to register atexit which run at interpreter teardown and often the loop is gone.

ryan: solution: provide `safe_close_sync(client)` that spawns a short-lived loop in a new thread to run `client.aclose()` and swallows interpreter-teardown errors. Document that app frameworks should prefer proper shutdown handlers though.

doc-bot: Suggestion created: DEVEX-3507: "Python SDK: lifecycle helpers (lifespan installer, safe_close_sync), deprecate naive asyncio.run shim, add lazy client proxy and typing stubs".

mike: also add a debug opt-in: `REDWOOD_SDK_LIFECYCLE_DEBUG=1` that logs a one-time warning when an AsyncClient is created outside an active lifespan, including a short stack excerpt. That should help users find module-scope creations without noisy default logs.

zara: +1. For quickstart we should update samples to use the helper and add a troubleshooting section: "Hangs after code reload / Task was destroyed" with checklist: module-scope clients, asyncio.run in startup, atexit cleanup.

deploy-bot: CI: added integration test that starts uvicorn --reload and asserts no pending tasks after restart. Test flake reproduced locally. :construction_worker:

ryan: i'll open a small PR with the lifespan helper, the safe close util, and a docs patch. will keep the API tiny and opt-in for the debug logs.

zara: thanks all — that should stop a few support tickets.
